acceptance_criteria.criterion: Active run with matching queue entry shows live status card, kill button, and inline log preview.
Active run without matching queue entry shows log preview and CLI kill suggestion (no kill button).
Log preview cleanup functions are invoked on re-render or navigation.
Polling is registered via Router._setPolling() and cleaned up on route change.

summary: Enhanced project-detail.js with a queue-aware orchestrator section for active runs.
Added _pdLogPreviewCleanups module-level registry; drained at the start of each renderProjectDetail() call.
For active runs: calls API.orchestratorGetQueue() to find a matching entry (by logFilename), then renders OrchestratorWidgets.renderStatusCard() + kill button DOM element + inline log preview.
For active runs with no queue match: renders CLI kill hint + log preview; no kill button.
Non-active runs rendered unchanged via the existing run-event HTML structure.
Polling registered via Router._setPolling(pollQueue, 5000) when an active run is present.
Added 13 new tests to project-detail-runs.test.ts covering all 5 AC (AC-1 through AC-5).
All 29 tests pass (16 existing + 13 new); full GUI suite 610 tests / 21 files, zero regressions.

comments.note: gui/public/views/project-detail.js: The renderRunsList() function is defined as a nested closure inside the getRunLogs().then() callback. This prevents it from being unit-tested in isolation. Future refactoring could extract it as a module-level helper (accepting sorted, slug, activeFilename as parameters) to improve testability and reduce closure depth.

gui/public/views/project-detail.js: The queue match uses logFilename === activeFilename (strict equality). If the filename representation ever differs (e.g., path prefix vs basename), the match would silently fail. A comment noting this assumption would help future maintainers.
No other issues found in the touched files. Code is clean and consistent with existing SPA patterns.

summary: PASS. All 5 ACs verified through prior pipeline artifacts and line-by-line source review.

Three _pdLogPreviewCleanups drain sites are correctly placed with try/catch per entry: at renderProjectDetail() entry (navigation/full re-render), at renderRunsList() entry (queue poll re-render), and at pollQueue() entry (before re-fetch). All three are required and all defensive.
Queue match (logFilename === activeFilename strict equality) is correct for the current data shape where both values are JSONL basenames. Known assumption is appropriately flagged.
Router._setPolling(pollQueue, 5000) correctly called only when activeFilename is truthy; non-active runs do not register polling.
Kill button callback re-polls the queue after a successful kill and re-renders. This provides correct immediate UI feedback.

comments.note: No blocking issues found. All 5 ACs verified through prior pipeline artifacts and line-by-line source review.

The pollQueue function drains _pdLogPreviewCleanups before re-fetching, and renderRunsList() also drains the array at its entry. The double-drain is harmless (draining an already-empty array is a no-op) since pollQueue calls renderRunsList immediately after. Accepted as correct and robust.

Queue match uses strict equality: queue[i].logFilename === activeFilename. Both values come from the same filename format (JSONL basename) via their respective API calls. The match is correct for the current data shapes. The assumption is documented as a Developer flag; no change needed.

[documentation-forward] renderRunsList() is a nested closure inside the getRunLogs().then() callback. The file-level or section-level comment should note this as a known refactor candidate (extract as module-level helper accepting sorted, slug, activeFilename) to guide future contributors.
